passages.p1: Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best answer to each of the following questions from 1 to 10. [I] Artificial intelligence, often abbreviated as AI, is the evolution of computer systems capable of performing tasks that traditionally demanded human intelligence, such as linguistic interpretation and decision-making. [II] By employing intricate mathematical algorithms, AI empowers machines to handle extensive data and replicate various functions of the human brain. [III] The remarkable precision and efficiency of AI have led to its extensive adoption across various fields. [IV] AI-powered robots are becoming increasingly helpful in different industries. To illustrate, industrial robots have gained widespread use in tasks such as heavy transporting and product assembly in manufacturing. These robots are meticulously engineered to operate with exceptional precision and speed, consequently increasing productivity in factories. Additionally, AI-equipped rescue robots have been designed for emergency situations, capable of making intelligent decisions to navigate in hazardous surroundings, which means that they can replace human rescuers in disaster areas. AI has also been integrated into people's daily gadgets. Private digital assistants, for instance, can comprehend and respond quickly to users' voice commands, which is highly valuable for basic tasks like searching for information online or scheduling appointments. Moreover, relying on traditional maps for directions is becoming outdated as people now can use AI-driven navigation apps. With real-time data processing, those apps can identify the quickest and most time-efficient routes to a destination; as a result, they help users save lots of time. Furthermore, diet trackers, another type of AI application, offer nutritional advice that specifically meets individual requirements. AI is significantly reshaping our routines and personal habits. AI is growing so rapidly that it's revolutionised different industries and changed our daily lives. Therefore, more helpful and extraordinary AI applications are expected to emerge in the years to come. (Adapted from Bright)
passages.p2: Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the option that best fits each of the numbered blanks from 11 to 15. Many animals around the world are on the brink of extinction due to habitat destruction and human activities. The panda, as an example, (11) ____________. As one of the most iconic symbols of conservation, pandas face immense challenges in their survival. Pandas, (12) ____________, are facing critical threats worldwide due to deforestation and habitat loss. As forests are cleared for agriculture, urban development, and logging, the resources pandas rely on are rapidly disappearing. This global issue affects not only pandas but also countless other species that share these ecosystems. Efforts to save pandas have increased over the years, with many organizations focusing on breeding programs and habitat restoration. (13) ____________. Additionally, stricter laws have been implemented to combat illegal logging and land exploitation. These measures aim to give pandas a fighting chance at survival. Protected by strict conservation policies, (14) ____________. Although there has been some progress, more effort still needs to be made to secure their future. (15) ____________. This is essential for giving this beloved species a chance to flourish again.
passages.p3: Read the following passage and mark the letter A, B, C, or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best answer to each of the following questions from 16 to 23. In today's world, we have different kinds of media available to us at all times, but did you know that the history of media actually goes back millennia? The word ‘media' refers to the different ways in which people transmit information. By this definition, we can say with confidence that human beings created the first type of media around 64,000 years ago when we first began painting simplistic symbols on the walls of caves. Since then, the more we have evolved, the more advanced our media have become. According to experts, it was sometime around 3,400 BC when human beings first began utilising written language as a means of communication. For generations, apart from verbal communication, people had to write everything manually until the mid-1440s. It was Johannes Gutenberg which revolutionised media when he created an invention called the printing press. This marked the beginning of what we now call "mass media": Gutenberg's innovative invention made print media like books, newspapers and magazines at a large scale and much information with a wider audience than ever before. Several hundred years after the invention of the printing press, during the 19th century, we created cameras and later, the radio. The invention of the radio began the age of broadcast media, and the development of television swiftly followed it. This allowed many people to watch fascinating movies, programmes and documentaries, all of which remain popular today. In the 2000s, we saw the rise of digital media. Now, we visit web pages, listen to podcasts, stream music and communicate on social media using our smartphones. We even use QR codes to share information instantly. We have come a long way, and so have the ways we communicate! (Adapted from Bright)

passages.p6: Read the following leaflet and mark the letter A, B, C, or D on your answer sheet to indicate the correct option that best fits each of the numbered blanks from 35 to 40. How to Avoid Negative Social Media Content Social media offers inspiration, yet it also spreads harmful posts which (35) ____________ your mood and thinking. Protecting your mental well-being requires conscious strategies. Practical Tips ● Try to (36) ____________ profiles that circulate hostility or constant criticism. ● Learn to (37) ____________ manipulative headlines and sensational claims before they affect your emotions. ● Develop healthy online habits by following communities that encourage learning, kindness, and creativity. In other words, if a community gives off negative vibes, look for (38) ____________ that promotes positivity and creativity. ● Reduce screen time if you notice too (39) ____________ negativity, since it can easily drain motivation. ● Pause before you respond to aggressive comments; sometimes silence preserves peace of (40) ____________. Negative content can be pervasive, but choosing wisely ensures your digital world remains calmer, safer, and more productive.
